findings.reason: the done-when greps the literal under `reckon/` and requires `_plan_html.py` alone, so an inaccurate owner census is exactly the input that makes the instrument's exhaustiveness unverifiable; correcting the count and deriving it from a grep of the literal rather than by hand changes the section's instrument.
findings.text: §17 says "the card's class literal has three owners today beyond the store", then names and the code holds exactly two (`plan_review.py:208` tests `"section-landed"` inline; `doccheck.py:116` defines `_LANDED_SECTION_CLASS`), so the plan's own owner census is already short before the instrument is built — the same undercount §17 says "was an undercount at every review of this design"

findings.reason: the interface as written is smaller than the behaviour it must hide and pushes the wrapper context back onto each caller, so the section must either widen the signature to take the enclosing element or state that the streaming parser passes the wrapper's attributes and that `_AuthoredProseParser`'s existing section stack (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:189`) supplies them.
findings.text: §16 specifies the identity rule as "a pure function over a tag's name and attributes" and says the prose parser "calls it at every heading it streams", but the case that rule exists to resolve is the wrapper-id section, whose identity sits on the enclosing `<section id=...>` and not on the h2, which is why `_wrapper_section_heading` (reckon/_store.py:860) exists at all; a pure function over the heading tag's own name and attributes cannot see the wrapper's attributes

findings.reason: if the heading-tag function returns the raw authored id while routing's normaliser returns the canonical form, the same section has two identities, which is the drift the plan claims the single owner prevents; the section must route heading identity through `section_record_id` or state why the two derivations cannot diverge.
findings.text: §16 claims "one identity remains, computed by one owner", but `section_record_id` in `reckon/crew/routing.py:215` already derives the one identity every spelling of a section addresses (normalising `§5.1` to `s5-1`) and `section_id_candidates` beside it reconciles a heading id `s5.1` with the dotted and hyphenated spellings, while the new heading-tag function and the span parser would derive identity from authored HTML by a rule of their own; the plan lists routing.py only as a walk to rewrite and never reconciles the two derivations

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §16 specifies the section-identity rule as "a pure function over a tag's name and attributes", which is narrower than the wrapper-id resolution that already lives in `reckon/_store.py:860` `_wrapper_section_heading` — see FINDING.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16 and §17 place section identity in `reckon/_plan_html.py` and claim "one identity remains, computed by one owner", but `reckon/crew/routing.py:215` `section_record_id` already owns the section-identity derivation and the plan names it only as a consumer to rewrite, never as an owner to reconcile with.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 states one public definition is added and why nothing else can be retired, §17 names the private heading walks it retires (net one), §18 names the private `_plan_remaining_sections` it retires (net one), and no section adds a CLI option, MCP view or refusal family — §16's refusal reuses the existing `plan-review-missing` family and names the uncovered sections in its detail.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched well and cites machinery that exists (`_StructuredSectionSpanParser` and `structured_section_spans` in `reckon/_plan_html.py`; `read_trees`, `call_name`, `literal_strings`, `definitions`, `_staged_writes` and `interfaces` walking `ast.walk(tree)` in `reckon/interface_counts.py`), but its census of the card-class literal's owners is a hand count that is already wrong, and §17 states the very failure mode (a hand-written list undercounts) one paragraph before committing it.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §16 exposes the identity rule for the streaming `_AuthoredProseParser` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:162`), which cannot consume offset spans, and §17 keeps `structured_section_spans` for the store's boundary contract while adding one richer reader; neither layer is added without a stated reason the existing reader cannot carry it.
